newsitem.title: INDIA: PRESS DIGEST - Indian newspapers - March 19.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Indian newspapers - March 19.

text.p: Following is a summary of major Indian business and political stories in leading newspapers prepared for Reuters by Business News and Information Services Pvt Ltd, New Delhi Tel:3324842, 3351006, 3761233 Fax:+91-11-3351006 Internet: biznis@giasbm01.vsnl.net.in
Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
TOP STORIES
The Hindustan Times
PARLIAMENT CANNOT CURB JUDICIAL REVIEW POWER

Parliament cannot divest constitutional courts of the power of judicial review even by way of a constitutional amendment, a constitution bench of the Supreme Court ruled. The court, in an unanimous judgement, said the power of judicial review over legislative action vested in the high courts under the constitution is an integral and essential feature of the constitution, and forms part of its basic structure. The seven-judge bench was presided over by the chief justice.
The Times Of India
PROPOSAL TO MAKE POLL EXPENSE PAPERS PUBLIC

The Election Commission is contemplating making election expenditure accounts of political parties public, as a step towards bringing about transparency in the funding of elections. The commission has also proposed matching the accounts not only with the income-tax returns filed by the political parties but also with the returns filed by their respective candidates to detect suspected fudging. All seven national parties and most of the regional parties have submitted their accounts for last year's general election.
The Pioneer
JUDGES BILL DEFERRED

Faced with opposition from the Left and the Bharatiya Janata Party, the United Front (UF) government deferred the controversial bill seeking to restore the executive's say in appointments and transfer of judges. Almost simultaneously, it gave up its bid to revalidate discretionary quotas of ministers. The government's rethink on the Constitution amendment Bill on judges came after Left parties threatened to stall it.
The Economic Times
MOODY'S REPORT HARSH: MORGAN

Morgan Stanley gave Indian corporate debt a "buy" rating, contradicting Moody's assessment which downgraded India's sovereign credit rating. Morgan Stanley said Moody's, which called the country's creditworthiness "unfavourable", was unduly harsh on India. The "buy" rating was given in a recent report issued by Morgan Stanley's team of credit analysts for fixed income investors.
NEW EXPLORATION POLICY TO FUEL INVESTMENT FLOW

The new exploration licensing policy (NELP) was announced for companies investing in oil and gas exploration. The NELP incorporated incentives such as reduction in royalty rates, abolition of cess, exemption of import duty for state-owned oil companies at par with private firms and creation of a hydrocarbon development fund. The new policy was viewed by experts as the first step towards dismantling the regulated regime in the petroleum sector.
FIVE PCT RISE IN INDUSTRIAL PRODUCTION

The 24-sector industrial production index, covering 50 percent of Indian industry, rose by five percent in January, as compared to the same month in 1996. The index increased by 4.9 percent between April 1996 and January 1997 compared to the corresponding period in the previous year.
Financial Express
MITTALS, JINDALS, ICCL, FACOR GET SHARE IN SUKHINDA MINES

The Orissa government decided to distribute at least 50 percent of the surplus 855 hectares chromite mining area in the Sukhinda valley among four ferro alloys companies. However, the mineral would be available only for captive use. The Sukhinda valley bears about 98 percent of the chrome ore reserves of the country.
Business Standard
NIDHIS, CHIT FUNDS BARRED FROM OVERSEAS FUNDS

The Reserve Bank of India barred nidhis (non banking financial companies) and chit funds from issuing rights and bonus shares to non resident Indians (NRIs) and overseas corporate bodies (OCBs) on a non repatriable basis. Nidhis formed a largely unregulated segment of the financial services sector, mobilising deposit schemes at unsustainably high interest rates.
INTERCONNECT CHARGES CUT BY 46 PCT

The Department of Telecommunications (DoT) slashed interconnect charges by 46 percent from 56,000 rupees per 30 channel link to 30,000 rupees. The new rate marked a 77 percent drop from the initial 136,000 rupees per link proposed in the previous year. Interconnect charges were paid to DoT for linking the private operators' exchanges with the government ones. DoT, however, said it reserved the right to appeal to the Telecom Regulatory Authority over the low charges.
LEFT TO SUPPORT BILL ON PRIVATE ROLE IN POWER TRANSMISSION

The Left parties of the ruling coalition decided to vote with the government on the bill providing for private participation in electricity transmission, despite reservations. The Left felt that though the bill would encourage multiplicity of authorities in the transmission sector and introduce anarchy and disfunction in the power grid system, it would not be advisable to table a cut motion on the issue.
The Observer
$400 MLN MORE DEBT FUNDS SET FOR CLEARANCE

The bourse regulator (SEBI) cleared $500 million worth debt funds by five foreign institutional investors (FIIs) through the 100 percent debt fund route. SEBI was also in the process of clearing $400 million debt funds by another four FIIs. The recent decision to allow FIIs to invest in dated government securities was seen as the reason for the flurry of applications by foreign investors.
Business Line
REVENUE TARGET WAY OFF MARK

The Finance Ministry seemed way off the mark in achieving the revenue target fixed for the current year. The ministry would need to collect direct taxes to the tune of 119.81 billion rupees before the end of the 1996/97 fiscal (April-March). Figures provided in the Finance Ministry's annual report showed that against the revised estimates of 398.53 billion rupees slated for the current fiscal, actual collections up to February were to the tune of 278.72 billion.
